member.name: T:SysWeaver.Parser.ExpressionEvaluator
member.summary: The standard expression evaluators and helpers. The standard evaluators support the operators "+ - * / %" (and unary "+ -"), parentheses, "," as the function argument separator, and all public static functions, constant fields and read only properties of that only use the evaluator type, with the name of the member (ex: "Sin", "Max", "PI"). Overloads are selected by the number of arguments (ex: "Log(8)" and "Log(8, 2)"). Function, constant and parameter names are case sensitive (ordinal comparison): "pi" is not "PI", so it can be used as a parameter name. The and evaluators add "^" (power, right associative), "<<" and ">>" (multiply / divide by a power of 2). The and evaluators add the bit operators "<< >> & ^ |" ("^" is XOR) and the unary "~" and "!" (both bitwise not). Precedence (high to low): unary operators, "^" (power), "* / %", "+ -", "<< >>", "&", "^" (XOR), "|" (the integer operators use the same order as C#). Numbers are parsed with the invariant culture (the current culture is never used), "0x" (hexadecimal), "0b" (binary) and "0o" (octal) prefixes are supported (the prefixes are case insensitive).

member.summary: Evaluator using Int64 arithmetics (unchecked: overflows wrap around, division by zero throws a when evaluated)

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Parser.ExpressionEvaluator.UInt64
member.summary: Evaluator using UInt64 arithmetics (unchecked: overflows wrap around, division by zero throws a when evaluated). The unary minus is not supported (use "0-x")

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Parser.ExpressionEvaluator.Decimal
member.summary: Evaluator using Decimal arithmetics (overflows and division by zero throw when evaluated). "x^y" is computed exactly (by repeated multiplication) when y is an integer, else using on the values converted to Double. "x<<y" is x * 2^y and "x>>y" is x / 2^y (computed the same way)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.ExpressionOptimizer.Optimize(System.Linq.Expressions.Expression)
member.summary: Optimizes a linq expression (repeated until nothing changes): binary operations and static method calls with constant arguments are evaluated (constant folding), "x + 0", "x - 0", "x * 1", "x / 1", "x | 0", "x ^ 0" become "x", "x * 0", "0 * x", "x & 0" and "0 << x" become 0, "0 - x", "x * -1" and "x / -1" become "-x" (not for unsigned types), conversions to the same type are removed, conditionals with a constant test are replaced by the taken branch, and nodes that are equal to a node seen before (by this or an earlier optimization) are replaced by that shared node (parameters are never merged). For floating point types (Half, Single, Double) "x * 0", "0 * x" and "0 - x" are kept as is (x * 0 is NaN if x is NaN or infinite, 0 - 0 is +0 but -0 is -0). The other floating point rules are kept, they differ from IEEE arithmetic only in the sign of a zero result (by design, expr-cov-17): "x + 0" and "0 + x" give -0 for x = -0 (IEEE: -0 + +0 = +0), and "x - c" with a -0.0 constant c (also matched as 0) gives -0 for x = -0 (IEEE: +0). NaN and infinities give the same result as the unoptimized expression; "x * 1", "1 * x", "x / 1", "x * -1", "-1 * x" and "x / -1" are exact (they're not folded for Half). For Decimal the folded result has the same value, but may have a different scale (ex: 1.5m + 0.00m is 1.50m unoptimized, 1.5m optimized; 1.5m * 0m is 0.0m unoptimized, 0m optimized). Constant folding runs the operation when optimizing, so exceptions (ex: an integer division by zero) are thrown by this method.
member.param: The linq expression to optimize
member.returns: An optimized version of the expression
member.exception: The expression is null (DEBUG builds only)
